newsitem.title: UK: Latin America stays focus for sugar freight inquiries.
newsitem.headline: Latin America stays focus for sugar freight inquiries.

text.p: Latin American origins again formed the focus of demand on the sugar freight market on Monday as a number of new orders and fixtures emerged, shipbrokers said.
Genoc quoted for 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Cuba to a number of European destinations, including Baltic, Casablanca, Portugal, Mediterranean and Black Sea for 24/28 February.

Cargill was open for 8,000 tonnes in bulk from Thailand to Japan for 1/5 March and Andre was open for 8,500/12,000 tonnes in bags from Acajutla to east or west Africa or Red Sea for the second half of February.

Czarnikow Rionda quoted for 14/17,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Buenaventura to east Africa/Colombo for prompt/seven days and also for 13/13,600 tonnes from Thailand to Indonesia for February 27/March 5.
The same charterer was said to have fixed 20/21,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Buenaventura to California for prompt loading. Further details have yet to emerge.
CSC was in the market for 10,800/10,900 tonnes of bulk sugar from La Romana to US Gulf/Atlantic for 14/24 February.
Masters Shipbroking issued an account order for 12,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Goa and Kandla to Novorossisk for prompt/February 15 dates.
Firmer business included E D & F Man, which was said to have fixed 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from France to Iran for prompt shipment.

Shipbrokers said Vitol booked tonnage to transport 21,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Cuba to Morocco with options of Egyptian Mediterranean and Black Sea for mid-February. The ship was said to be called Amity Union.
